key_insight: A transformer-based decoder can learn coherent-information limits for quantum error correction and use them to approach optimal threshold performance.
engineering_relevance: This suggests machine-learning decoders can both estimate when a QEC code will fail and improve logical error suppression in practical surface-code systems.
method: Train a transformer with maximum-likelihood decoding objectives to predict coherent information and logical operator uncertainty.
Evaluate on surface code under code-capacity, phenomenological, and circuit-level noise models.
Add soft post-selection to filter low-confidence outputs using MLD cosets.
evidence_signal: The model accurately predicts coherent information, matches known threshold limits, and outperforms minimum-weight perfect matching in logical error rate.
watch_item: Performance and threshold estimates may depend on noise-model assumptions and the calibration of confidence-based post-selection.
paper_title: Machine Learning Optimal Quantum Error Correction Thresholds
